## Trial `rootless-container-service-rhel1__2ogV9Pe`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: the app runs rootless under appsvc, serves on port 8080, and a genuine bounded reboot test (distinct pre/post boot IDs, disconnect during restart, and full post-reboot recovery of service, container, HTTP response, and process ownership) confirms it starts at boot without an active appsvc login session. The independent lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and the new listening socket on 8080. Hygiene is good overall; the only ding is leftover diagnostic residue (/tmp/rhkey.gpg and dnf/pull logs) from a GPG troubleshooting detour that turned out unnecessary once the plain retry succeeded.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.900 | 27/0 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Containerized web application runs as the unprivileged appsvc account (rootless)
  - **Why:** appsvc (uid 1000, non-root) was created and used to pull and run the nginx:alpine container rootlessly via podman/Quadlet. Post-reboot process inspection confirms the nginx master process (pid 915) is owned by appsvc, not root, demonstrating the running container is truly unprivileged.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1908868aece548a8`, `cmd-fd85c74254f34ebf`, `cmd-9be533e57f4c4483`, `cmd-5d0d2daf93674330`, `cmd-b59aa218944e443b`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Application serves on port 8080
  - **Why:** Quadlet unit publishes PublishPort=8080:80; podman ps shows 0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp; curl to the node on 8080 returns HTTP 200 both before and after a full reboot; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms a listening socket on *:8080 owned by the pasta rootless network helper.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5d0d2daf93674330`, `cmd-0740bb0934684363`, `cmd-b17087e3edb34fe5`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
  - **Why:** Full bounded reboot transition was captured, not just configuration: healthy baseline (linger enabled, generator-created default.target.wants symlink, webapp active, HTTP 200, boot_id 03408ac4...) -> reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect -> node unreachable during restart -> new boot_id cbea0e05... confirming an actual reboot -> recovered state showing no interactive login session for appsvc (loginctl shows only the lingering user-manager entry, session count reduced from 2 to 1 and no tty/pts session), user@1000.service active, webapp.service active, container auto-started, HTTP 200, and nginx process owned by appsvc.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6a4e8ea8c6be4644`, `cmd-963d013d874a453a`, `cmd-6df7859ad13b4414`, `cmd-4dc06296899f4320`, `cmd-db00ca6d35924e57`, `cmd-8c2d47a5d8ea4733`, `cmd-561adbda40184e04`, `cmd-c8474170bcec4b08`, `cmd-b17087e3edb34fe5`, `cmd-b59aa218944e443b`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands map directly to the task: user/linger creation, podman install, image pull, Quadlet unit creation, firewalld port opening, and the reboot itself. One troubleshooting excursion was not clearly load-bearing: after the first podman install attempt failed on a transient dnf GPG-parsing error (cmd-b36cafac70154729), the executor ran `gpg --dearmor` on the RHEL release key into /tmp/rhkey.gpg (cmd-da30be3b205249ea) as a diagnostic experiment; the subsequent successful install (cmd-0ceb776b90b04a8f) used the normal dnf/GPG path and did not depend on that dearmored key, so the mutation appears unnecessary. Its residue (/tmp/rhkey.gpg) and the diagnostic dnf logs (/tmp/dnf_install.log, /tmp/dnf_install2.log, /tmp/pull.log) are confirmed still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot rather than cleaned up. This is low-risk, bounded, and non-destructive (no security weakening, no service disruption), but it is retained residue from a failed troubleshooting path rather than fully restored.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-b36cafac70154729`, `cmd-da30be3b205249ea`, `cmd-0ceb776b90b04a8f`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Only a single reboot cycle was captured for node1 (the only managed node), so no additional restart cycles were available to further corroborate stability of the boot autostart mechanism.
- The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare was disabled), so the prepare-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison.
- Systemd `--user enable` reported the unit as generated/transient, which is expected for Quadlet-generated units; boot autostart instead relies on the generator's default.target.wants symlink, confirmed present and functioning across the observed reboot.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
